questions.stem: CDMA differs from GSM in that CDMA
options: uses only one fixed frequency for all users in a country
gives each call its own code
questions.explanation: Code Division Multiple Access gives each call a spreading code; GSM uses time and frequency division.

questions.explanation: The NCC regulates telecommunications, licensing operators and assigning spectrum.

questions.explanation: The keyboard is an input device for typing data; the monitor, printer and speakers are output devices.

questions.explanation: EDGE (Enhanced Data rates for GSM Evolution) improved on GPRS speeds.

questions.explanation: The memory unit (flash/RAM) holds software and data.

questions.explanation: The microphone is a transducer from sound to electrical signals.

questions.stem: The ringer (buzzer) of a phone is the component that
options: stores the subscriber number and contacts
converts radio waves to sound in the ear
questions.explanation: The ringer/loudspeaker produces ringtones; the vibrator gives silent alerts.

questions.stem: A game or banking program installed on a phone is an example of

questions.stem: Fitting a screen protector and a rugged case to a new phone is
questions.explanation: These steps are taken before damage happens, so they are preventive.

questions.stem: One advantage of regular preventive maintenance of phones is that it
options: removes the need for a battery
makes the phone free of charge
extends the life of the phone
questions.explanation: Preventing faults extends service life and reduces repair costs.

questions.stem: Replacing a cracked display after a customer drops a phone is
questions.explanation: Corrective maintenance restores equipment after a fault has occurred.

questions.stem: In BGA re-balling, the stencil is used to
options: cut the PCB tracks around the chip
place new solder balls on the chip pads
questions.explanation: The stencil aligns solder balls on each pad before reflow with hot air.

questions.stem: A technician should NOT eat or drink at the repair bench mainly because
options: it slows the computer and the soldering iron
spills and solder residues are hazards
questions.explanation: Spilled liquid damages boards and lead/flux residues can be swallowed.

questions.stem: Soldering fumes in a phone workshop are best controlled by
options: a fume extractor or good ventilation
blowing the fumes with the mouth
questions.explanation: Flux fumes irritate the airways; extraction and ventilation remove them.

questions.stem: A customer says the other person cannot hear her during calls, though she hears them well. The part MOST likely faulty is the
questions.explanation: If the outgoing voice is missing, the mouthpiece circuit is suspected first.

questions.stem: A touch screen responds only in some areas after a phone was dropped. The likely fault is a
options: blocked network on the SIM card
questions.explanation: The digitiser senses touch; cracks cause dead zones.

questions.stem: A phone asks for a "phone lock code" that the owner has forgotten. This is a
questions.explanation: Security lock prompts are software issues, solved by approved reset or unlocking procedures.

questions.stem: When reassembling a phone, the flex cables should be connected
options: after the battery is connected and the phone switched on
by pressing with a hot iron
before final screwing, checking each is seated
questions.explanation: Connectors are seated with the battery out, checked, and the case closed without pinching.

questions.topic: Tracing and Fault Finding in Hardware
questions.stem: With the battery out, the resistance between a phone board's VBAT and ground reads 0 Ω on the multimeter. This indicates
options: an open circuit in the earpiece speaker
a short on the battery line
questions.explanation: Zero ohms means a dead short, often a shorted capacitor or PMIC, which must be located.

questions.topic: Tracing and Fault Finding in Hardware
questions.stem: Injecting a known signal at a point and checking whether it appears further along the circuit is called
questions.explanation: Signal injection and tracing locate the stage where a signal is lost.

questions.stem: A phone keeps restarting by itself every few minutes even with a new battery. The FIRST software remedy to try is
options: replacing the SIM socket on the board
questions.explanation: Restart loops are often caused by corrupted settings or apps; a reset (and if needed reflash) is tried before hardware work.

questions.explanation: Capital is the money/assets invested to set up the business.

questions.topic: Facilities and Equipment for Mobile Phone Workshop
questions.stem: An anti-static mat on the repair bench is provided to
options: discharge static electricity safely and protect components
questions.explanation: ESD mats bleed charge to earth slowly, protecting sensitive ICs.

questions.topic: Tracing and Fault Finding in Hardware
questions.stem: A phone board powered from a bench supply draws 0 mA when the power key is pressed, though VBAT is present at the PMIC. The NEXT check should be
options: the power key line and its voltage at the PMIC
the colour of the back cover
questions.explanation: If VBAT is present but nothing draws current on pressing power, the power-on (PWR key) signal path to the PMIC is checked next.

questions.stem: Explain the following terms: (a) call forwarding [2 marks] (b) MMS [2 marks] (c) quad-band phone [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) diverting incoming calls to another number when busy, unreachable or unanswered
2 marks: (b) Multimedia Messaging Service: sends pictures, audio and video between phones
2 marks: (c) phone that can operate on four GSM frequency bands (e.g. 850/900/1800/1900 MHz), usable in many countries
questions.explanation: Call forwarding diverts calls; MMS carries multimedia; quad-band phones work on four GSM bands for worldwide roaming.

questions.stem:
(a) Name three electronic components found on a mobile phone circuit board. [3 marks]
(b) State one function of each component named in (a). [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) any three: resistor, capacitor, diode, transistor, IC, inductor/coil, crystal (1 each)
3 marks: (b) matching function: resistor limits current; capacitor stores charge/filters; diode allows one-way current/protection; transistor switches/amplifies; IC performs complex functions; crystal sets clock frequency (1 each)
questions.explanation: Resistors limit current, capacitors filter, diodes rectify/protect, transistors switch, ICs process, crystals set clock.

questions.topic: Common Tools and Equipment for Hardware and Software Repairs
questions.stem: State the use of each of the following in a phone repair workshop: (a) hot-air rework station [2 marks] (b) DC power supply with ammeter [2 marks] (c) magnifying lamp or microscope [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) removing and refitting SMD and BGA components by blowing controlled hot air
2 marks: (b) powering the board without battery and showing current drawn, to diagnose shorts or dead sets
2 marks: (c) inspecting tiny components and solder joints for cracks, corrosion or bridges
questions.explanation: Hot air reworks SMD/BGA chips; a bench supply with ammeter powers and diagnoses boards; magnification allows inspection of joints.

questions.stem:
(a) What is flashing a mobile phone? [2 marks]
(b) State two reasons for flashing a phone. [2 marks]
(c) State two precautions before flashing a customer's phone. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) re-installing/updating the firmware (operating software) using a computer, box or software tool
2 marks: (b) any two: hanging/restart loop, corrupted software, upgrade, remove virus, change language/region (1 each)
2 marks: (c) any two: back up customer data, charge battery fully, use correct firmware for the model, ensure stable power (1 each)
questions.explanation: Flashing reloads firmware to fix corrupted software or upgrade. Back up data, charge battery, use the exact firmware and stable power.

questions.stem:
A customer brings a phone that does not charge.
(a) State three possible hardware causes. [3 marks]
(b) Describe three steps to diagnose the fault. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) any three: faulty charger/cable, dirty or damaged charging port, faulty battery, damaged charging IC/PMIC, broken track (1 each)
3 marks: (b) test with a known-good charger and cable; inspect and clean the port; measure charging voltage/current at the port and battery with meter or USB tester (1 each)
questions.explanation: Causes: charger, port, battery, charging IC, tracks. Diagnose by substitution, inspection/cleaning and measurement.

questions.stem:
A technician buys a screen for ₦22,000, charges ₦7,500 for labour and adds 10% of the parts cost for overheads.
(a) Calculate the total cost of the repair. [3 marks]
(b) If the customer is charged ₦35,000, calculate the profit. [1 mark]
(c) State two risks in running a phone repair business. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) overhead = 10% of 22,000 = ₦2,200
2 marks: (a) total = 22,000 + 7,500 + 2,200 = ₦31,700
1 mark: (b) profit = 35,000 - 31,700 = ₦3,300
2 marks: (c) any two: theft/loss of customers' phones, damage during repair, fake parts, power cost, fire (1 each)
questions.explanation: Overhead ₦2,200; total ₦31,700; profit ₦3,300. Risks include theft, damage, fake parts and power costs.
